W1.subject: Welcome to Just In Case — your first step takes 2 minutes
W1.html:
You're in. Your plan is 9 short templates, one at a time. Today, just the first. ͏ ͏ ͏

Welcome aboard · 2 min to set up

Thank you for doing the thing most people put off.

Hi {first_name},

Your plan is made up of 9 short templates — simple Google Docs that you copy into your own Google Drive. We’ll send them one at a time, each with a small step, so it never feels like a lot. Today, just the first one: your Cover Sheet.

Copy Template 1: Cover Sheet →

Your copy is yours. It lives in your Google Drive and we never see what you write in it. You'll need to be signed in to Google — when prompted, click Make a copy.

Use a personal Google account, not a work one — work accounts can be shut off when you change jobs, and your employer can see them. No account? Create one free with your existing email.

Rather have all 9 at once? They’re listed at the bottom of this email.

Start here

Your first step takes two minutes.

Open your Cover Sheet and fill in three boxes: your name, today’s date under Originally Created, and the same date under Last Updated. That’s the whole step.

I did it — what's next?

If you’d like smaller steps now or in the future, you can switch to one 2-minute question at a time, emailed twice a week.

Your next few weeks

Each email tells you exactly what to do. Here’s a little of what’s ahead:

In 3 days

Read This First

What to do first, who to contact, and who looks after the pets.

 15 min
Week 1

Legal & decision making

Where your will and other legal documents are kept.

 15 min
Week 2

Digital access

Your passwords, your phone, and the codes that come by text.

 15 min
Week 3

Financial snapshot

Bank accounts, cards and loans, investments, and keys.

 25 min
Week 4

Home, car & everyday life

Mortgage or rent, car loan, and the bills that must keep getting paid.

 25 min

Then Insurance, ID & Records and Personal Notes, followed by two final steps to print and store your plan — about 9 weeks in total. But it's your plan and your pace: skip ahead, take a week off, or come back whenever you're ready. See the whole plan →

Have a question? The FAQ is a good place to start. Otherwise, see you in 3 days for the next step — we're so glad you're here.

Here's to a long life, well organized.
— The Just In Case team

4  Pet care

W10.subject: Your plan should work when nothing else does (15 min)
W10.html:
Phones die and passwords change. Paper doesn't need either. ͏ ͏ ͏
Your plan Step 10 of 11
  
See the whole plan →

Step 10 of 11 · Print a paper copy · About 15 min

Now make one copy that works without a password.

Hi {first_name},

Your plan lives safely in Google Drive — but the people who need it might not be able to get in. A printed copy in a binder works even when nothing else does.

1  Print it

Open each of your 9 templates, then File → Print. Single-sided is easier to update.

2  Check your Cover Sheet date one last time

Before you print, make sure Last Updated shows today’s date. That’s how everyone knows which version is the latest.

3  Put it in a binder

Cover Sheet on top, then Templates 2 to 9 in order. We like this binder with these folders that fit inside it — though any sturdy binder will do the job. (Affiliate links — we may earn a small commission.)

Open my templates to print →
Not now? Add to calendar

No printer at home? Use one at a trusted friend’s or family member’s house. We don’t recommend libraries or copy shops — these pages hold account numbers and other private details, and it’s easy to leave one behind.

Keep it current

When something changes — a new bank, a new phone, a new baby:

1Update the relevant template.
2Reprint just that page and swap it into the binder.
3Change Last Updated on your Cover Sheet, and reprint that page too.

Life gets busy, and updating your plan is easy to put off — that’s completely normal. You don’t need to keep track of it all. For as long as you’re on the Premium Plan, we’ll check in twice a year with a short, guided review, so your plan stays current and your family stays covered.

W11.subject: Last step: put it somewhere safe, and let your people know where (15 min)
W11.html:
A plan nobody can find can't help. Fifteen minutes and you're done. ͏ ͏ ͏
Your plan Step 11 of 11
  
See the whole plan →

Step 11 of 11 · Store it & tell someone · About 15 min

Last step: put it somewhere safe, and let the people who’ll need it know where to find it.

Hi {first_name},

Pick the place that fits your life. The best spot is safe from fire and water, but easy for the right person to reach.

1  A fire-resistant home safe

Easy to update and reach. Make sure someone knows the code or where the key is.

2  Your lawyer or executor

Many will hold a sealed copy for you, often at no cost.

3  A bank safe deposit box

Very secure, but it can take time for family to get access — best as a second copy.

Mark my plan complete →
Not now? Add to calendar

Then tell two trusted people where it is — here’s how.

Name two trusted contacts

Pick two people who’d step in first — a partner, an adult child, a sibling, a close friend. Two, so if one can’t be reached, the other can.

Send each of them this

“I’ve put together a plan for my family, just in case anything ever happens to me. The paper copy is kept [where]. There’s also a digital copy in my Google Drive. You’re one of two people I’ve told — the other is [name]. Nothing to do now, I just wanted you to know where it is.”

Email this to them →

Optional: give them access to the digital copy. In Google Drive, right-click your Just In Case folder, choose Share, and add their email as a Viewer. Only you and the people you choose can see it — not us.

What happens after today

Your plan is done. We’ll help you keep it that way.

For as long as you’re on the Premium Plan, you’ll get:

✓Two checkpoints a year — a short review at six months and at one year, so nothing quietly goes out of date.
✓A guided option, if you want one — instead of one checklist email, we’ll walk you through the checkpoint one short question at a time, spread over a couple of weeks. Just opt in when your checkpoint arrives.
✓A monthly newsletter — clear, helpful guides for the moments most people are never prepared for, like a what-to-do-when-someone-dies checklist, closing accounts after a death, or how to talk to your family about your plan. Every article is also on our website, so you can opt out of the newsletter any time and keep your checkpoints. No other extra emails.

Prefer just one review a year? Switch to a single yearly checkpoint — we’ll skip the six-month one and cover everything at the one-year mark. You can switch back any time.

CP1.subject: Six months on: is anything out of date? (15 min)
CP1.html:
Your six-month check-in. Most people are done in 15 minutes. ͏ ͏ ͏
Checkpoint Six-month review
  

Six-month checkpoint · About 15 min

Six months on: is anything out of date?

Hi {first_name},

It’s been six months since you last updated your plan. Things change quietly — a new password here, a new account there. This is a quick look to catch them. Every update means one less thing for your family to figure out.

You don’t need to reread everything. Just check these:

Passwords & your phone

Changed a password manager, a phone or a carrier? Update the Digital Access Plan.

Who to contact

Any new numbers, or someone you’d add or remove? That’s in Read This First.

New accounts or cards

Opened or closed anything? Update your Financial Snapshot.

Bills & autopay

Any new subscriptions or changed providers? See Home, Car & Everyday Life.

Open my plan →

Don’t skip this part

Your checkpoint isn’t finished until your binder is updated.

1.Print every template you changed. The full page, not just the part you edited.
2.Print your Cover Sheet with today’s date in Last Updated. Print it even if nothing else changed.
3.Put both in your binder and throw away the old pages.

Your family will use the paper copy, so it has to match what’s on your computer.

Big change since last time?

These usually touch more than one template:

A new baby — name a guardian (Legal & Decision Making), update beneficiaries and coverage (Insurance & Protection), and maybe add a note (Personal Notes).
A new job — new health or life insurance (Insurance & Protection) and a new retirement account (Financial Snapshot).
A move — mortgage or rent, bills and providers (Home, Car & Everyday Life), and where your papers are kept.
A change in your relationship — beneficiaries, your will and healthcare directive, and who to contact.
A change in who you’d turn to — Who To Contact and pet care (Read This First), plus anyone named in your legal documents.

Prefer a hand? Get this checkpoint as 5 quick questions, one every few days. Same checklist, smaller pieces.

CP2.html:
Your yearly check-in. Most people are done in 15 minutes. ͏ ͏ ͏
Checkpoint Annual review
  

Annual checkpoint · About 15 min

Time for your quick annual review

Hi {first_name},

It’s time for your annual review. Keeping your plan up to date is one of the kindest things you can do for the people who’ll need it. This checkpoint covers the things that tend to change once a year.

Check these, and update anything that’s changed:

Insurance renewals

New policy numbers, providers or coverage amounts? Update Insurance & Protection.

Beneficiaries

Still the right people on your life insurance, retirement and POD accounts? Check Insurance & Protection, Financial Snapshot and Read This First.

Legal documents

Signed or changed a will, trust or directive? Update Legal & Decision Making.

Tax returns & ID

Add the latest tax return, and check any renewed passport or license in Identification & Records.

Personal notes

Anything you’d add to a letter, or someone new to tell? Update Personal Notes.

Open my plan →

1.Print every template you changed. The full page, not just the part you edited.
2.Print your Cover Sheet with today’s date in Last Updated. Print it even if nothing else changed.
3.Put both in your binder and throw away the old pages.

Your family will use the paper copy, so it has to match what’s on your computer.

On one checkpoint a year? Also check:

Your phone and passwords (Digital Access Plan), who to contact (Read This First), any new accounts or cards (Financial Snapshot), and bills or providers that changed (Home, Car & Everyday Life).
